t: What Brain-Inspired Spiking Neural Networks Is
title: What Brain-Inspired Spiking Neural Networks Is
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Brain-inspired spiking neural networks (SNNs) are AI models that compute like neurons: they communicate with discrete spikes over time instead of continuous activations. Information lives in spike timing and rates, enabling ultra-efficient event-driven computation. This record is the entry point of the teaching ladder for Brain-Inspired Spiking Neural Networks: start here, then move through the research state, the specifications, the public developments, the open challenges, and finally each piece needed to build it.
key_points: Brain-Inspired Spiking Neural Networks in one line: Brain-inspired spiking neural networks (SNNs) are AI models that compute like neurons: they communicate with discrete spikes over time instead of continuous activations.
Why it matters: They are the software twin of neuromorphic hardware — and the path to AI that learns continuously like brains do..
Where it is used: neuromorphic chips, robotics, event-based vision, brain-computer interfaces, continual learning..
Ladder rank 1 — the foundation. Everything else builds on this.

# simulation — Neuron Model Library
# Field: Compounded
# --- setup ---
params = {'v': 0.0, 'threshold': 1.0, 'inputs': [0.3, 0.4, 0.5]}
# --- run ---
v = params['v']
spikes = 0
for x in params['inputs']:
    v = 0.9 * v + x
    sp = v >= params['threshold']
    spikes += sp
    v = 0.0 if sp else v
print('spikes:', spikes)
